question: Article 38 guarantees the right to form associations. What reasonable restrictions does the Constitution permit on this right?

options.A: Only associations with more than 500 members require government registration and approval
options.B: Restrictions imposed by law in the interests of morality or public order — the state can regulate or prohibit associations that threaten public morality or order
options.C: No restrictions whatsoever — all associations have absolute freedom under the Constitution
options.D: Only political parties can be restricted, while all other types of associations remain entirely free

explanation: Article 38 provides: 'Every citizen shall have the right to form associations or unions, subject to any reasonable restrictions imposed by law in the interests of morality or public order.' This means: (1) The state CAN restrict or even prohibit associations — but only through LAW; (2) The restrictions must be REASONABLE; (3) The permitted grounds are morality and public order; (4) Any restriction outside these grounds would be unconstitutional. The right is broad but not absolute.

question: How were Mukti Bahini fighters fed during extended operations away from border camps?

options.A: They carried military ration packs supplied by the United Nations through the Red Cross
options.B: They foraged for food in forests and survived on wild fruits and hunted game exclusively
options.C: They relied on local villagers who risked their lives to share food, and on supplies carried by volunteers through jungle trails and river routes
options.D: They received regular airdrops of food and supplies coordinated by the Indian Air Force

explanation: Mukti Bahini fighters operating inside Bangladesh relied primarily on civilian support for food. Bengali villagers, despite their own poverty and the risk of Pakistani reprisals, shared rice, vegetables, fish, and whatever food they had. Volunteers — often women and teenagers — carried supplies through jungle paths and river routes, evading Pakistani patrols. The fighters' survival depended on the solidarity of the civilian population, making the war a truly popular struggle.

question: Bangladesh has achieved remarkable food security, particularly in rice production. What key policy contributed most to tripling rice output since independence?

options.A: Large-scale import of rice from neighboring countries to ensure stable domestic supply
options.B: Expansion of irrigation enabling dry-season Boro rice cultivation with high-yielding varieties, along with fertilizer subsidies and government procurement at support prices
options.C: Government purchase of all farmland to establish collective state farms on the Soviet model
options.D: Conversion of rice fields to shrimp farms to generate foreign exchange for food imports

explanation: Bangladesh's rice production tripled from about 10 million tons at independence to approximately 38-40 million tons today, driven by: (1) EXPANSION OF IRRIGATION — particularly shallow tube wells enabling dry-season Boro rice, now the largest crop; (2) HIGH-YIELDING VARIETIES — developed by BRRI and BARI; (3) FERTILIZER SUBSIDIES — making inputs affordable for small farmers; (4) GOVERNMENT PROCUREMENT — providing price support. Rice self-sufficiency is one of Bangladesh's greatest development...

question: Article 42 requires compensation for compulsory acquisition of property. Can the adequacy of compensation be challenged in court?

options.A: Yes, the courts can fully review whether compensation is adequate and increase it if found insufficient
options.B: No, Article 42(2) explicitly provides that the adequacy of compensation shall not be questioned in any court
options.C: Only the Supreme Court can review compensation adequacy, and only in death penalty cases
options.D: Compensation can be challenged only if it is less than half the market value of the acquired property

explanation: Article 42(2) provides that Parliament shall determine the compensation for compulsory acquisition, and 'no provision of any such law shall be called in question in any court on the ground that the compensation provided is not adequate.' This is a significant limitation — while the state MUST provide compensation, the courts cannot review whether the amount is sufficient. The legislature has the final say on what constitutes adequate compensation. This reflects a deliberate constitutional cho...

question: Sector 11 had to manage large-scale civilian displacement. How did the Mukti Bahini handle the refugee crisis in this sector?

options.A: They directed civilians to stay in their homes regardless of Pakistani attacks, refusing to assist evacuation
options.B: They assisted civilians fleeing toward India, provided escorts through dangerous areas, and helped organize refugee camps across the border in Meghalaya and Assam
options.C: They relocated all civilians to the Sundarbans where they were safe from Pakistani patrols
options.D: They evacuated civilians by air using helicopters provided by the Soviet Union

explanation: Sector 11 forces operated in an area with massive civilian displacement toward India. The Mukti Bahini: (1) Provided escorts for groups of civilians fleeing Pakistani reprisals; (2) Guided refugees through safe routes to the Indian border; (3) Coordinated with Indian authorities and international organizations to establish refugee camps in Meghalaya and Assam; (4) The refugee flow provided cover for guerrilla infiltration — fighters moved with civilian groups. The humanitarian and military di...

question: Why was the Radcliffe Award published two days AFTER the independence of India and Pakistan?

options.A: Radcliffe had not finished drawing the boundary and needed extra time to complete his work
options.B: Lord Mountbatten deliberately delayed publication until 17 August 1947 to avoid the British being held responsible for the chaos and violence that would follow
options.C: The printing press broke down and the maps could not be reproduced in time for independence day
options.D: Both India and Pakistan requested the delay to allow more time for population transfer arrangements

explanation: The Radcliffe Award was ready by 12 August 1947, but Lord Mountbatten, the last Viceroy, deliberately withheld publication until 17 August — two days AFTER independence (15 August). Mountbatten admitted in later interviews that he wanted to avoid British responsibility for the inevitable communal violence that would follow the boundary announcement. By delaying, the British could claim the violence occurred in independent India and Pakistan, not under British rule. This decision has been heav...

question: The Padma River is notorious for bank erosion. Which district has been most severely affected by Padma erosion in recent decades?

options.A: Shariatpur and Madaripur on the south bank, which have lost significant land and infrastructure to the encroaching river
options.B: Rajshahi on the north bank, where the river has destroyed the historic city's waterfront
options.C: Dhaka on the east bank, threatening the capital's southern suburbs and industrial zones
options.D: Pabna on the west bank, where the river has consumed entire villages and agricultural land

explanation: The south bank of the Padma — particularly Shariatpur, Madaripur, and Faridpur districts — has experienced severe erosion. The Padma has been gradually shifting southward, consuming land, villages, and infrastructure. Notable impacts include: (1) Displacement of hundreds of thousands of people; (2) Loss of agricultural land; (3) Destruction of roads, schools, and other infrastructure; (4) The shifting course threatened the Padma Bridge project site. Riverbank erosion is one of Bangladesh's mo...

question: Bangladesh Bank requires banks to allocate a specific percentage of their loan portfolio to SME financing. What is the purpose of this requirement?

options.A: To reduce the overall lending capacity of banks and control inflation in the economy
options.B: To redirect all bank lending away from large corporations and exclusively toward small businesses
options.C: To ensure that small and medium enterprises, which employ the majority of the workforce, have access to formal credit rather than relying on informal moneylenders
options.D: To create a special fund that the government can borrow for infrastructure projects at low interest

explanation: Bangladesh Bank's mandatory SME lending targets aim to: (1) Address the credit gap for SMEs, which are the backbone of employment but often lack collateral for traditional bank loans; (2) Promote inclusive economic growth by ensuring formal financial access for small businesses; (3) Reduce SME dependence on informal moneylenders who charge exorbitant interest rates; (4) Banks must allocate a percentage of their total loans to the SME sector. This is part of Bangladesh Bank's financial inclusi...

question: Sector 1 included Cox's Bazar. What strategic significance did this coastal area have during the war?

options.A: It was the primary landing site for weapons shipments from the Soviet Union
options.B: It contained Pakistan's only oil refinery, making it a critical target for sabotage
options.C: It provided an alternative supply route through its long coastline, and its beach could serve as a potential amphibious landing zone for joint forces
options.D: It was the location of the Pakistan Army's Eastern Command headquarters

explanation: Cox's Bazar, with its 120 km coastline, had strategic significance: (1) Its long beach and proximity to Myanmar offered an alternative supply route; (2) It could serve as a potential amphibious landing zone for Indian naval forces; (3) The coastal area allowed maritime infiltration by Mukti Bahini fighters; (4) The area's relative isolation from main Pakistani force concentrations made it suitable for guerrilla operations. The Cox's Bazar-Teknaf peninsula was part of Sector 1's vast operation...

question: How is the President of Bangladesh elected?

options.A: By direct popular vote of all citizens through a nationwide election
options.B: By the members of Parliament in a special session, as provided in Article 48
options.C: By an electoral college consisting of all members of Parliament and all elected local government representatives
options.D: By the Chief Justice and senior judges of the Supreme Court in a special constitutional ceremony

explanation: Article 48(1) provides that the President shall be elected by the members of Parliament. This is consistent with Bangladesh's parliamentary system where the President is the constitutional head of state, elected by the legislature rather than directly by the people. The election requires a majority of the total members of Parliament. The President holds a largely ceremonial role, with executive power vested in the Prime Minister and Cabinet who are responsible to Parliament.

question: Sector 2 included Dhaka city. What made urban guerrilla operations in Dhaka particularly dangerous compared to rural sectors?

options.A: The rural sectors faced more danger because Pakistani forces concentrated their strength outside the capital
options.B: Dhaka was the Pakistani military headquarters with the highest concentration of troops, checkpoints, and intelligence operatives — making every operation extremely high-risk with limited escape routes
options.C: Dhaka's population was hostile to the Mukti Bahini, providing no safe houses or support to fighters
options.D: Dhaka had no guerrilla activity at all because the city was completely locked down throughout the war

explanation: Urban guerrilla operations in Dhaka were exceptionally dangerous because: (1) Dhaka was the Pakistani military headquarters — the highest concentration of troops, military police, and intelligence agencies; (2) Checkpoints and patrols were ubiquitous; (3) The dense urban environment offered limited escape routes if an operation was compromised; (4) Informants and collaborators increased the risk of betrayal. Despite these dangers, the Crack Platoon and other operatives conducted sabotage, pro...

question: Bangladesh has held leadership positions in UN peacekeeping missions. Which role has a Bangladeshi national notably held?

options.A: Commander of the UN Peacekeeping Force in Cyprus, one of the longest-running UN missions
options.B: UN Under-Secretary-General for Peace Operations, the highest peacekeeping position at UN headquarters
options.C: Force Commander of the United Nations Mission in Sierra Leone and other missions, with several Bangladeshi generals leading major UN operations
options.D: Chair of the UN Security Council's Peacekeeping Sub-Committee on a permanent basis

explanation: Several Bangladeshi military officers have served as Force Commanders of major UN peacekeeping missions, including: (1) Lieutenant General Chowdhury Hasan Sarwardy — Force Commander in Sierra Leone (UNAMSIL); (2) Other senior Bangladeshi officers have commanded missions in Côte d'Ivoire, Liberia, Sudan, and other locations. This reflects the trust the UN places in Bangladeshi peacekeepers and the country's stature as a leading troop contributor with over 175,000 personnel deployed since 1988.

question: Article 36 guarantees freedom of movement throughout Bangladesh. On what grounds can this right be restricted?

options.A: Only during a proclaimed state of emergency, with no restrictions permitted in normal times
options.B: Reasonable restrictions imposed by law in the public interest — such as curfews, restricted areas, or quarantine zones
options.C: Only with the individual's written consent, making all movement restrictions voluntary
options.D: Movement can be restricted only for convicted criminals serving sentences of imprisonment

explanation: Article 36 provides: 'Subject to any reasonable restrictions imposed by law in the public interest, every citizen shall have the right to move freely throughout Bangladesh, to reside and settle in any place therein and to leave and re-enter Bangladesh.' The state CAN restrict movement through laws serving the public interest — examples include curfews during civil unrest, restricted military areas, quarantine during epidemics, or bail conditions requiring an accused to remain in a specific area.

question: Major C. R. Dutta commanded Sector 4 throughout the war. What characterized his leadership style?

options.A: An authoritarian command style that discouraged input from junior officers and local volunteers
options.B: A preference for large-scale conventional battles over guerrilla tactics, leading to high casualties
options.C: A democratic leadership approach that empowered his fighters and built strong relationships with local communities along the border
options.D: A distant command style that delegated all operations to subordinates while he remained at headquarters

explanation: Major C. R. Dutta was known for his democratic, inclusive leadership style. As one of the few Hindu Bengali officers, he built strong rapport with both his fighters and the local communities along the Khasi Hills border. His approach: (1) Empowered junior officers and guerrilla leaders to take initiative; (2) Maintained close relationships with the Khasi and Jaintia communities who provided shelter and guides; (3) Led by example rather than from behind. His post-war work as a minority rights ...

question: Which Mughal Subahdar of Bengal built the famous Lalbagh Fort in Dhaka?

options.A: Islam Khan Chishti, who also established Dhaka as the Mughal capital of Bengal in 1610
options.B: Mir Jumla, who conquered Assam and expanded Mughal territory to the northeast
options.C: Prince Azam began the fort and Shaista Khan continued it, but it remained incomplete after Pari Bibi's death
options.D: Murshid Quli Khan, who later moved the capital to Murshidabad in the early 18th century

explanation: Lalbagh Fort was begun in 1678 by Prince Muhammad Azam (son of Emperor Aurangzeb) during his brief tenure as Subahdar. When Shaista Khan succeeded him, he continued construction but halted it after the death of his beloved daughter Iran Dukht (Pari Bibi), whose tomb stands in the central mausoleum. The fort remains incomplete to this day — with three main structures: the Diwan-i-Aam, the Pari Bibi Mausoleum, and the three-domed mosque.

question: The Lower Meghna estuary is one of the widest rivers in the world. What is its approximate width near the Bay of Bengal?

options.A: About 5 kilometers, similar to the width of the Padma at the bridge site
options.B: About 20 kilometers — a vast expanse of water with numerous chars and islands
options.C: About 2 kilometers, making it easily bridgeable with modern engineering
options.D: About 50 kilometers, forming a true inland sea that is visible from space

explanation: The Lower Meghna estuary, formed by the combined waters of the Padma, Jamuna, and Meghna rivers, widens to approximately 20 kilometers near the Bay of Bengal. This vast waterbody contains numerous char islands and sandbars, constantly shifting due to erosion and accretion. The estuary's immense width and powerful tidal currents make it one of the most dynamic and challenging river systems in the world. No bridge has been built across the Lower Meghna due to these engineering challenges.

question: Bangladesh Bank regulates e-commerce payment systems. What requirement exists for e-commerce payment gateways?

options.A: All e-commerce payments must be processed through government-owned banks exclusively
options.B: Payment gateways must obtain a license from Bangladesh Bank and maintain transaction records for regulatory compliance
options.C: E-commerce payments are unregulated and operate without any central bank oversight
options.D: Only foreign payment gateways are allowed to operate, with domestic providers prohibited

explanation: Bangladesh Bank requires e-commerce payment gateways to: (1) Obtain a license or authorization; (2) Maintain proper transaction records for regulatory compliance; (3) Implement security measures including two-factor authentication; (4) Comply with anti-money laundering and KYC requirements; (5) Report suspicious transactions. The regulatory framework was strengthened after the 2021 e-commerce fraud scandals involving companies like Evaly, which exposed gaps in payment system oversight.

question: Sector 5 operated along the Dawki-Tamabil corridor in eastern Sylhet. What terrain challenge did this sector face compared to the other Sylhet sectors?

options.A: It was located in the flat floodplains of the Surma River with no hills or forests for cover
options.B: It was situated on the border with Myanmar, facing a completely different set of geographic obstacles
options.C: It straddled the Khasi Hills border where steep terrain and dense forests made supply movement extremely difficult, and the Dawki road was the only reliable transport artery
options.D: It was located entirely within Indian territory, requiring special diplomatic clearance for all operations

explanation: Sector 5's defining terrain challenge was the steep, forested Khasi Hills border area. The Dawki-Tamabil road was the only reliable transport artery through this rugged terrain — all other routes were footpaths through dense forest. This meant: (1) Both Pakistani and Mukti Bahini forces were tethered to the single road; (2) Supplying guerrilla units operating away from the road was extremely difficult; (3) The terrain gave advantage to the defender — but Sector 5's knowledge of alternative fo...

question: Does the President of Bangladesh enjoy immunity from criminal prosecution while in office?

options.A: Yes, the President has complete immunity from all criminal and civil proceedings during their term
options.B: No, the President can be prosecuted for any crime like any ordinary citizen
options.C: Article 51 provides that the President shall not be answerable to any court for acts done in the exercise of official duties, but criminal prosecution may be possible after impeachment
options.D: The President has immunity only for traffic violations, with full liability for all other criminal acts

explanation: Article 51(1) provides: 'Without prejudice to the provisions of article 52, the President shall not be answerable to any court for the exercise and performance of the powers and functions of his office or for any act done or purporting to be done by him in the exercise and performance of those powers and functions.' This provides immunity for OFFICIAL acts — but not for personal criminal conduct. If the President commits a crime outside official duties, they could potentially face prosecution...

question: Sector 6 shared its northern border with which Indian state that provided a rear base?

options.A: Tripura, which hosted the main refugee camps and Mukti Bahini headquarters
options.B: West Bengal, with Kolkata serving as the main logistics and command center
options.C: Assam and West Bengal — the sector bordered the narrow 'Chicken's Neck' corridor of India, providing access to supply routes from both states
options.D: Meghalaya, with Shillong serving as the primary training and logistics base

explanation: Sector 6 (Rangpur-Dinajpur) was unique in bordering both Assam and West Bengal along India's narrow 'Chicken's Neck' corridor (the Siliguri Corridor). This geographic position: (1) Provided access to supply routes from both Assam and West Bengal; (2) Allowed the sector to receive support from multiple Indian military formations; (3) Made the sector strategically important for controlling the northern approaches to Bangladesh. The Siliguri Corridor is a narrow strip of Indian territory connect...

question: Dhaka frequently ranks among cities with the worst air quality globally. What is the primary source of Dhaka's air pollution during winter?

options.A: Vehicle emissions from the city's millions of cars and motorcycles operating daily
options.B: Industrial emissions from garment factories and tanneries concentrated in the city center
options.C: Brick kilns surrounding the city that burn coal and wood, combined with construction dust and transboundary pollution from neighboring regions
options.D: Natural dust storms from the Arabian Desert that reach Bangladesh during the winter months

explanation: Dhaka's winter air pollution is primarily driven by: (1) THOUSANDS OF BRICK KILNS around the city that operate seasonally and burn coal, wood, and other fuels with no emission controls; (2) CONSTRUCTION DUST from the city's constant building boom; (3) TRANSBOUNDARY POLLUTION from India's industrial regions that drifts across the border; (4) Vehicle emissions and industrial sources contribute but are secondary. The winter temperature inversion traps pollutants near the ground, creating the haz...

question: The Supreme Court has interpreted Article 32 to include the right to a healthy environment. In which landmark case was this established?

options.A: Dr. Mohiuddin Farooque vs. Bangladesh, where the Court held that the right to life includes the right to a pollution-free environment
options.B: Anwar Hossain Chowdhury vs. Bangladesh, the 8th Amendment case establishing the basic structure doctrine
options.C: Masdar Hossain vs. Bangladesh, the case that established judicial separation from the executive
options.D: Asaduzzaman Siddiqui vs. Bangladesh, the 16th Amendment case on judicial removal

explanation: In Dr. Mohiuddin Farooque vs. Bangladesh (1996), also known as the 'BELA case,' the Supreme Court held that the right to life under Article 32 encompasses the right to a healthy environment. The case was filed by the Bangladesh Environmental Lawyers Association (BELA) challenging a flood control project that threatened wetlands. question: Sector 8 civilians actively resisted Pakistani forces. What form did civilian resistance take in the Kushtia-Jessore region?

options.A: Civilians formed armed militias, attacked Pakistani patrols, cut communication lines, and provided intelligence to Mukti Bahini forces operating in the sector
options.B: Civilians remained entirely passive, taking no action against Pakistani forces throughout the war
options.C: Civilians collaborated exclusively with Pakistani forces, providing them with intelligence about Mukti Bahini
options.D: Civilians fled to India immediately, leaving the sector depopulated for the entire duration

explanation: The Kushtia-Jessore region witnessed significant civilian resistance: (1) Armed villagers formed local militias (lashkar) that attacked isolated Pakistani patrols; (2) Civilians cut telephone and telegraph lines to disrupt Pakistani communications; (3) Farmers and shopkeepers provided food, shelter, and intelligence to Mukti Bahini fighters; (4) Women hid weapons and acted as couriers. The civilian resistance was so intense that Pakistani forces conducted brutal reprisals, burning villages an...

question: The Chittagong Armoury Raid of 1930 was led by Surya Sen. What happened to Surya Sen after the raid?

options.A: He escaped to India and lived in exile until Bangladesh's independence in 1971
options.B: He was captured in 1933, tried, and executed by hanging in 1934, becoming a martyr for the independence movement
options.C: He surrendered to British authorities and was given a life sentence, later released in 1947
options.D: He was killed during the raid itself, dying in a gun battle with British forces

explanation: After the 1930 Chittagong Armoury Raid, Surya Sen (Masterda) evaded capture for nearly three years, continuing to organize revolutionary activities. He was finally arrested in February 1933, tried for sedition and waging war against the King-Emperor, and sentenced to death. He was executed by hanging on 12 January 1934 in Chittagong Central Jail. His sacrifice made him one of the most revered martyrs of the Indian independence movement, particularly in Bengal.

question: The Surma and Kushiara rivers reunite to form the Meghna River. Where does this confluence occur?

options.A: Near Chandpur, where the combined flow meets the Padna estuary before entering the Bay
options.B: Near Sunamganj, at the heart of the haor wetlands in northeastern Bangladesh
options.C: Near Bhairab in Kishoreganj district, where the two branches of the Barak River merge into the mighty Meghna
options.D: Near Mymensingh, where the Old Brahmaputra joins the Meghna river system

explanation: The Surma (northern branch) and Kushiara (southern branch) of the Barak River reunite near Bhairab in Kishoreganj district to form the Meghna River. From Bhairab, the Meghna flows southward, receiving the combined flow of the Padma and Jamuna near Chandpur, before emptying into the Bay of Bengal as the vast Lower Meghna estuary. The Bhairab confluence is the point where the two daughters of the Barak River become the mighty Meghna.

question: Bangladesh Bank operates the National Payment Switch (NPS). What is the primary function of the NPS?

options.A: Processing all international wire transfers between Bangladeshi banks and foreign financial institutions
options.B: Interconnecting all banks' ATM and POS networks, enabling customers to use any bank's ATM regardless of where their account is held
options.C: Managing the government's salary payments to all public sector employees across ministries
options.D: Operating the stock exchange's electronic trading platform for securities settlement

explanation: The National Payment Switch (NPS), operated by Bangladesh Bank, is the central infrastructure that interconnects all commercial banks' ATM networks and Point of Sale (POS) terminals. Key functions: (1) Allows a customer of Bank A to withdraw cash from Bank B's ATM; (2) Routes and settles interbank transactions; (3) Forms the backbone of Bangladesh's electronic payment ecosystem. The NPS has significantly improved customer convenience and reduced the need for cash transactions.

question: Sector 9 relied heavily on civilian boats. How did local fishermen contribute to Mukti Bahini operations?

options.A: They donated their boats and navigated the treacherous waterways, using their knowledge of tides and channels to move fighters and supplies undetected
options.B: They refused to help either side, keeping their boats hidden throughout the war
options.C: They sold their boats to Pakistani forces at inflated prices to fund the Mukti Bahini
options.D: They abandoned their boats and fled to India, leaving the waterways unusable

explanation: Local fishermen were indispensable to Sector 9 operations: (1) They donated their boats or served as boatmen for Mukti Bahini fighters; (2) Their intimate knowledge of the maze of rivers, creeks, and tidal patterns enabled safe movement; (3) They could navigate at night and in bad weather when Pakistani patrols were less active; (4) Their fishing activities provided cover for reconnaissance missions. The fishermen of the southwestern delta were the unsung heroes of Sector 9.

question: Article 43 protects the privacy of home and correspondence. What is required for a lawful search of a private residence?

options.A: Only the verbal permission of the homeowner, which can be given at any time
options.B: Authorization in accordance with law — such as a search warrant issued by a competent court
options.C: Approval from the local elected representative, such as the Mayor or Union Parishad Chairman
options.D: A written order from the Prime Minister's Office countersigned by the Cabinet Secretary

explanation: Article 43 provides that every citizen shall have the right to be secure in their home against entry, search, and seizure 'save in accordance with law.' This means: (1) A search can only be conducted when authorized by a VALID LAW; (2) Typically, a search warrant issued by a magistrate under the Code of Criminal Procedure is required; (3) Warrantless searches are permissible only in specific circumstances defined by law (e.g., hot pursuit, imminent destruction of evidence). Arbitrary or unaut...

question: The naval commandos of Sector 10 operated without uniforms. Why was this significant under international humanitarian law?

options.A: It had no legal significance, as all combatants were treated equally regardless of attire
options.B: Operating without uniforms meant they could be treated as spies or saboteurs rather than prisoners of war if captured, increasing the risks they faced
options.C: It gave them automatic protection under the Geneva Conventions as civilian non-combatants
options.D: It exempted them from all laws of war, allowing them to use any methods without restriction

explanation: Under international humanitarian law (particularly the Geneva Conventions), combatants who operate without distinctive uniforms or insignia recognizable at a distance may be denied prisoner of war status if captured. The naval commandos, operating in civilian clothes to blend in and approach targets, faced this risk. If captured, Pakistan could potentially treat them as unlawful combatants or spies rather than prisoners of war entitled to Geneva Convention protections. Despite this risk, the ...

question: Bangladesh annually sends mangoes to India as part of 'mango diplomacy.' Which Bangladeshi mango variety is most famously gifted?

options.A: Langra from Rajshahi, known for its green skin and exceptionally sweet, fiberless flesh
options.B: Himsagar from Khulna, recognized by its golden color and intense fragrance
options.C: Haribhanga from Rangpur, a large, fleshy mango with a distinctively round shape
options.D: Fazli from Rajshahi, a large variety weighing up to a kilogram, famous for its size and sweetness

explanation: Haribhanga mangoes from Rangpur have become the most famous variety used in Bangladesh's 'mango diplomacy' with India. The Haribhanga is known for its large size, sweet taste, and distinctive round shape. Bangladesh also gifts Hilsa fish to India during Durga Puja. India reciprocates with sweets during Eid. This tradition of food diplomacy reinforces the cultural bonds between the two Bengali-speaking regions across the border.

question: The transitional provisions in the Fourth Schedule of the Constitution served what primary purpose?

options.A: To establish permanent emergency powers for the military in case of future conflicts
options.B: To provide legal continuity by retaining existing laws and officials from the Pakistan period until the new constitutional order was fully operational
options.C: To abolish all laws from the Pakistan period and create an entirely new legal system from scratch
options.D: To transfer all government authority to the United Nations until elections could be held

explanation: The transitional provisions in the Fourth Schedule of the 1972 Constitution served to ensure legal continuity during the transition from the wartime provisional government to the permanent constitutional order. Key provisions: (1) Existing laws from the Pakistan period remained in force (unless inconsistent with the Constitution); (2) Civil servants, judges, and officials continued in their posts; (3) The Constituent Assembly transformed into the first Parliament; (4) Legal proceedings contin...

question: Z Force was named after Major Ziaur Rahman. When was Z Force formed as the first Mukti Bahini brigade?

options.A: In March 1971, immediately after the Declaration of Independence was broadcast
options.B: In mid-1971, as Bengali defectors from the Pakistan Army were organized into formal brigade structures with Indian assistance
options.C: In December 1971, just days before the final victory and surrender of Pakistani forces
options.D: After independence in 1972, as part of the reorganization of the Bangladesh Army

explanation: Z Force was formed in mid-1971 as the first organized brigade of the regular Mukti Bahini. As Bengali officers and soldiers defected from the Pakistan Army and gathered in India, they were organized into three brigades: Z Force (Ziaur Rahman), K Force (Khaled Mosharraf), and S Force (K. M. Shafiullah). Each brigade was named after the first letter of its commander's name. Z Force operated primarily in the northern sectors.

question: The Royal Indian Navy Mutiny of 1946 shook British confidence in their hold on India. Which city was the epicenter of this mutiny?

options.A: Calcutta, where dock workers joined the mutiny and paralyzed the city's port operations
options.B: Chittagong, where Bengali sailors took control of several ships and raised the flag of independence
options.C: Bombay, where naval ratings revolted against poor conditions and British officers, spreading to other ports
options.D: Karachi, where the mutiny began among sailors on British warships in the Arabian Sea

explanation: The Royal Indian Navy Mutiny began on 18 February 1946 in Bombay (now Mumbai) when naval ratings (sailors) of HMIS Talwar protested against poor food, racial discrimination, and harsh treatment by British officers. The mutiny quickly spread to over 70 ships and shore establishments in Karachi, Calcutta, Madras, and other ports. question: Bangladesh's heat index combines temperature and humidity. Why is Bangladesh particularly vulnerable to high heat index values?

options.A: High altitude combined with intense solar radiation makes the air feel hotter than the thermometer reads
options.B: High humidity from the Bay of Bengal and numerous rivers prevents sweat evaporation, making the body feel much hotter than the actual temperature
options.C: Strong dry winds from the Himalayas cause rapid dehydration and increase the perceived temperature
options.D: Urban heat islands in Dhaka affect the entire country's climate, raising temperatures nationwide

explanation: Bangladesh's location near the Bay of Bengal and its vast network of rivers create persistently high humidity levels. The heat index (which combines temperature and humidity) often reaches dangerous levels because: (1) High humidity prevents sweat from evaporating, the body's natural cooling mechanism; (2) Even moderate temperatures (32-35°C) can feel like 40-45°C+ when humidity exceeds 70-80%; (3) This is particularly dangerous for outdoor workers, farmers, and construction laborers. question: Bangladesh Bank operates the Bangladesh Real-Time Gross Settlement system. What is the primary function of BD-RTGS?

options.A: Processing small-value retail payments between individual customers of different banks
options.B: Settling large-value interbank transactions in real time, reducing settlement risk for high-value payments
options.C: Managing international remittance transfers from overseas workers to their families
options.D: Operating the government's tax collection system through electronic fund transfers

explanation: The Bangladesh Real-Time Gross Settlement (BD-RTGS) system, operated by Bangladesh Bank, is designed for large-value, time-critical interbank payments. question: Sector 2 under Major Khaled Mosharraf shared a border with which Indian state?

question: Who composed the song 'Amar Sonar Bangla' as a protest against the 1905 Partition of Bengal?

question: The Barak River, which splits into the Surma and Kushiara in Bangladesh, originates in which Indian state?

question: The Tangail Airdrop on 11 December 1971 involved Indian paratroopers linking with Sector 11. What was the objective of this operation?

question: Kaderia Bahini operated independently alongside Sector 11. Why was Kader Siddique's force allowed to maintain autonomy rather than being absorbed?

question: Idrakpur Fort in Munshiganj was built during the Mughal period. What was its primary purpose?

question: The Kaptai Dam on the Karnaphuli River generates hydroelectric power. What is its installed capacity?

options.A: 50 MW, a small run-of-river project that supplies only the local hill communities
options.B: 230 MW, the only hydroelectric power plant in Bangladesh and a significant source of renewable energy
options.C: 1,000 MW, making it the largest power plant of any type in the country
options.D: 500 MW, supplied equally to Bangladesh and neighboring Indian states

explanation: The Kaptai Hydroelectric Power Station, located on the Karnaphuli River in Rangamati, has an installed capacity of 230 MW (five generating units). It was commissioned in 1962 and remains the only hydroelectric plant in Bangladesh. The Kaptai Dam created Kaptai Lake — the largest artificial lake in Bangladesh. While hydroelectricity is clean and renewable, the project's construction displaced over 100,000 people, predominantly from indigenous Chakma communities.

question: What is the term of office for the President of Bangladesh?

options.A: Four years from the date of the presidential election, with a two-term maximum
options.B: Five years from the date on which the President enters office, renewable for one additional term
options.C: Six years, after which the President must step down and cannot seek re-election
options.D: Seven years, aligning with the extended term for Supreme Court judges

explanation: Article 50(2) provides that the President shall hold office for a term of five years from the date on which they enter office. No person may hold the office of President for more than two terms, whether consecutive or not. The five-year term aligns with the normal duration of Parliament. The President continues in office until a successor enters office, even after the five-year term expires.

question: What is Bangladesh's rank among the world's apparel exporters?

options.A: First, the world's largest apparel exporter, ahead of China
options.B: Second, after China, making Bangladesh a dominant force in the global garment industry
options.C: Fifth, behind China, Vietnam, India, and Turkey in garment exports
options.D: Tenth, with a small but growing share of the global market

explanation: Bangladesh is the world's second-largest apparel exporter, after China and ahead of Vietnam, India, and Turkey. The RMG sector accounts for approximately 84% of Bangladesh's total export earnings, generating over $40 billion annually. With over 4 million workers (predominantly women), the industry is the backbone of Bangladesh's economy. The sector aims to reach $50 billion in exports and improve its position in the global value chain through diversification, value addition, and sustainability.

question: What happened to the laws that existed in East Pakistan before the 1972 Constitution came into effect?

All laws in force in East Pakistan before the Constitution continued to remain in force as 'existing laws' until altered, repealed, or amended by Parliament, provided they were consistent with the Constitution. This ensured: (1) No legal vacuum after independence; (2) The existing legal system continued to function; (3) Parliament could gradually reform laws. question: The British government's response to the 1943 Bengal Famine was widely criticized. What was a major failure of the relief effort?

options.A: The British government declared the famine a hoax and refused to provide any assistance
options.B: Wartime priorities took precedence — grain was diverted to the British Indian Army, the denial policy removed boats and food stocks from coastal Bengal, and relief was inadequate and delayed until millions had already died

question: The Teesta River water-sharing agreement between Bangladesh and India has been pending since 2011. What is the primary obstacle to finalizing this agreement?

options.A: Bangladesh has rejected the agreement because it demands 100 percent of the Teesta's water
options.B: The West Bengal state government in India has opposed the proposed 50:50 sharing formula, arguing it would harm farmers in northern West Bengal
options.C: The matter is pending before the International Court of Justice, preventing bilateral resolution
options.D: Both countries have agreed but are waiting for Chinese mediation before signing

explanation: The Teesta water-sharing agreement was initialed in 2011, proposing roughly equal sharing during the lean season. However, West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee has opposed the deal, arguing it would harm farmers in northern West Bengal. Since water is a state subject in India's federal system, the central government needs state consent. The agreement remains unsigned due to this domestic Indian political obstacle. Bangladesh has consistently sought the agreement's finalization.

question: Bangladesh Bank requires banks to maintain a minimum Capital Adequacy Ratio under Basel III. What does this ratio measure?

question: The Ganges-Brahmaputra-Meghna delta is the world's largest delta. Approximately what area does it cover?

options.C: About 500,000 square kilometers, extending across all of South Asia from the Himalayas to the sea
options.D: About 25,000 square kilometers, concentrated in the Sundarbans mangrove forest region

explanation: The Ganges-Brahmaputra-Meghna (GBM) delta is the world's largest delta, covering approximately 105,000 square kilometers. It is one of the most densely populated and agriculturally productive regions on Earth, but also one of the most vulnerable to climate change, sea level rise, and natural disasters.

options.D: The Anti-Corruption Commission after receiving a formal complaint from the President

explanation: Article 96(3) establishes the Supreme Judicial Council (SJC), composed of the Chief Justice and the two next senior judges of the Appellate Division. The SJC investigates allegations of proved misbehavior or incapacity against a Supreme Court judge. Only after the SJC recommends removal can Parliament vote on impeachment. This ensures judicial independence — judges are investigated by judges, not by the executive or legislature.

question: How did Pakistani forces attempt to counter Mukti Bahini operations in the open plains of Sector 6?

options.A: They deployed large numbers of tanks and armored vehicles to chase guerrilla units across the open fields
options.B: They relied on static checkpoints, village raids, and collective punishment to deter civilian support, but struggled against mobile guerrilla tactics
options.C: They built an extensive network of underground bunkers connected by tunnels spanning the entire sector
options.D: They negotiated local ceasefires with village leaders to create neutral zones free of combat

explanation: In the flat, open terrain of Sector 6, Pakistani counter-insurgency relied on: (1) Static checkpoints at key road junctions to control movement; (2) Raids on villages suspected of supporting the Mukti Bahini; (3) Collective punishment — burning homes and killing civilians to deter cooperation with guerrillas; (4) However, these brutal methods were ineffective against highly mobile guerrilla units that could strike quickly and disperse, often with the active support of the very villagers Pakis...

question: Alivardi Khan ruled Bengal from 1740 to 1756. What characterized his relationship with the British East India Company?

options.A: He expelled the British from Bengal entirely, closing all their trading posts and factories
options.B: He granted the Company complete sovereignty over Calcutta and the surrounding districts
options.C: He maintained a wary but pragmatic relationship — allowing the Company to trade while strictly limiting their military and political influence, and successfully resisting their attempts at expansion
options.D: He invited the British to station troops in his capital to protect against Maratha invasions

explanation: Alivardi Khan (reigned 1740-1756) was a strong and capable ruler who maintained Bengal's independence. He: (1) Allowed the British East India Company and other European powers to continue trading; (2) Strictly enforced limits on their fortifications and military activities; (3) Successfully defended Bengal against repeated Maratha invasions (which weakened his treasury); (4) His death in 1756 brought his young grandson Siraj-ud-Daulah to the throne, who lacked Alivardi's experience in managin...

question: The Jamuna River causes extensive bank erosion. Which engineering approach has been widely used to manage this erosion?

options.A: Dredging the riverbed to deepen the channel and reduce lateral erosion of the banks
options.B: Building concrete walls along the entire riverbank to create a permanent erosion-proof barrier
options.C: Constructing revetments and guide bunds using geo-bags and concrete blocks at vulnerable points, rather than attempting to control the entire river
options.D: Diverting the river's flow into artificial canals to reduce the volume passing through the main channel

explanation: Given the Jamuna's immense width (15-20 km during monsoon) and powerful flow, it is impossible to fully control or embank the entire river. The Bangladesh Water Development Board uses a 'selective intervention' approach: (1) REVETMENTS — sloped stone or concrete block coverings at critical erosion points; (2) GUIDE BUNDS — structures that direct flow away from vulnerable banks; (3) GEO-BAGS — large sand-filled bags used as temporary protection. These measures protect specific towns and infras...

question: Bangladesh Bank requires banks to classify loans based on repayment status. When does a loan become 'substandard'?

options.A: When the borrower misses a single monthly installment by even one day past the due date
options.B: When a loan remains overdue for 3 months or more, triggering mandatory provisioning requirements
options.C: When the borrower files for bankruptcy, regardless of whether payments have been missed
options.D: When the bank's internal review determines the borrower's business is no longer profitable

explanation: Under Bangladesh Bank's loan classification guidelines, loans are classified based on the duration of overdue: (1) STANDARD — repayments are regular; (2) SUBSTANDARD — overdue for 3 months or more; (3) DOUBTFUL — overdue for 6 months or more; (4) BAD/LOSS — overdue for 12 months or more. Banks must maintain provisions (reserves) against classified loans: 20% for substandard, 50% for doubtful, and 100% for bad/loss. This classification system ensures timely recognition of credit risk.

question: Pabna in Sector 7 witnessed notable civilian resistance. What role did Pabna's educated class play in the Liberation War?

options.B: They collaborated with Pakistani forces, serving as administrators in the occupation government
options.C: They remained completely passive, focusing on protecting their own property and families
options.D: They fled to West Pakistan at the start of the war and returned only after independence

explanation: Pabna's educated middle class — teachers, lawyers, doctors, and students — played a disproportionate role in organizing resistance: (1) Formed secret cells to distribute pro-independence propaganda; (2) Maintained communication links with the Mujibnagar Government; (3) Many crossed into India to receive military training; (4) Pabna's Edward College was a center of nationalist sentiment. The educated class provided organizational skills and ideological commitment that amplified the effectivene...

question: What is the current number of reserved seats for women in the Jatiya Sangsad?

options.A: 50 seats, filled by election by the 300 directly elected MPs based on proportional representation
options.B: 100 seats, with each political party required to nominate women for half their general seats
options.C: 25 seats, appointed directly by the Prime Minister from distinguished women citizens
options.D: 75 seats, equally distributed among the eight administrative divisions

explanation: Article 65(3) currently provides for 50 reserved seats for women in the Jatiya Sangsad. These seats are filled by election by the 300 directly elected MPs on the basis of proportional representation through the single transferable vote. The number was increased from 45 to 50 by the 15th Amendment (2011), and the provision was extended for 25 years by the 17th Amendment (2018).

question: Pakistani forces conducted brutal reprisals against civilians in Sector 8. What was the purpose of these reprisals?

options.A: To provide humanitarian assistance to villages affected by the ongoing military operations
options.B: To punish and terrorize civilians supporting the Mukti Bahini, through village burning, mass killings, and destruction of food stocks, aiming to sever the link between guerrillas and the population
options.C: To relocate all civilians to designated safe zones where they could be protected from combat
options.D: To collect taxes and revenue that had not been paid since the beginning of the conflict

explanation: Pakistani reprisals in Sector 8 were deliberately brutal, targeting the civilian population that supported the Mukti Bahini. Methods included: (1) Burning entire villages; (2) Mass executions of civilians; (3) Destruction of food stocks and crops; (4) The goal was to terrorize the population into withdrawing support from the guerrillas. However, these tactics largely backfired — the brutality drove more civilians to support the Mukti Bahini and fueled the flow of refugees into India.

question: Which major infrastructure project in Bangladesh is being built under China's Belt and Road Initiative?

options.A: The Padma Multipurpose Bridge, financed entirely by domestic resources without foreign loans
options.B: The Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant, built with Russian Rosatom technology and financing
options.C: The Karnaphuli Tunnel, the first underwater tunnel in South Asia connecting Chattogram's two banks
options.D: The Dhaka Metro Rail MRT Line-6, funded through Japanese JICA loans

explanation: The Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman Tunnel (Karnaphuli Tunnel) under the Karnaphuli River in Chattogram was built with Chinese financing and technical support under the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI). The 3.4 km tunnel, inaugurated in 2023, is the first underwater road tunnel in South Asia. Other major Chinese-funded BRI projects include the Payra Power Plant, the Dasherkandi Sewage Treatment Plant, and various road and bridge projects.

question: Article 70 causes an MP to lose their seat for voting against their party. Does this provision apply to votes on all matters, and are there any exceptions?

options.A: It applies only to votes on the budget and constitutional amendments, with all other votes exempt from the provision
options.B: It applies to all parliamentary votes without exception, requiring absolute party discipline in every division
options.C: It applies to voting in Parliament but does not prevent MPs from expressing dissent in parliamentary debates or committee proceedings, and some reform proposals suggest exempting non-confidence motions
options.D: It was repealed in 2018 and no longer applies to any parliamentary proceedings

explanation: Article 70 applies to VOTING in Parliament — an MP who votes against their party loses their seat. However, it does not prevent MPs from: (1) Expressing dissent in parliamentary debates; (2) Criticizing party positions in committee proceedings; (3) Advocating for policy changes within the party. Reform proposals have suggested creating exceptions for non-confidence motions, private members' bills, or conscience votes, but these have not been adopted. The provision remains one of the strictest...

question: Where did the limpet mines used by Sector 10 naval commandos originate?

options.A: They were captured from Pakistani naval stores during a daring pre-war raid on Chittagong port
options.B: They were manufactured in secret workshops in Kolkata by Bengali engineers who had fled the genocide
options.C: They were supplied by the Indian Navy, which provided the mines along with training in their use
options.D: They were purchased from international arms dealers through funds raised by the Concert for Bangladesh

explanation: The limpet mines used by Sector 10 naval commandos were provided by the Indian Navy, which also trained the Bengali volunteers in their use. The Indian Navy supplied the mines, diving equipment, and small boats necessary for the operations. The naval commandos did not capture, manufacture, or purchase their equipment — they were entirely dependent on Indian military support for their specialized weapons.

question: Besides Surya Sen, who were the two young women revolutionaries who participated in the Chittagong Armoury Raid?

Pritilata Waddedar led an attack on the Pahartali European Club in 1932 and, when cornered by police, consumed cyanide to avoid capture — becoming a martyr at age 21. question: What is the approximate total annual water discharge of Bangladesh's rivers into the Bay of Bengal?

options.A: About 100 billion cubic meters, similar to the annual flow of a single major European river
options.B: About 500 billion cubic meters, placing it among the top 20 river systems globally
options.C: Over 1,200 billion cubic meters, making the Ganges-Brahmaputra-Meghna system the second-largest river discharge in the world after the Amazon
options.D: About 3,000 billion cubic meters, exceeding even the Amazon River's discharge into the Atlantic

explanation: The combined discharge of the Ganges, Brahmaputra, and Meghna rivers is approximately 1,200-1,350 billion cubic meters annually — the second-largest river discharge in the world after the Amazon. This immense flow carries about 1 billion tons of sediment annually, building and maintaining the world's largest delta. The Brahmaputra alone discharges about 600 billion cubic meters, the Ganges about 500 billion, and the Meghna system about 150 billion.

question: The interest rate spread in Bangladesh's banking sector refers to the difference between what two rates?

options.A: The difference between the repo rate set by Bangladesh Bank and the interbank call money rate
options.B: The difference between the interest rate banks charge on loans and the interest rate they pay on deposits
options.C: The difference between Bangladeshi interest rates and international benchmark rates
options.D: The difference between fixed deposit rates for different maturity periods

explanation: The interest rate spread is the difference between the weighted average lending rate (what banks charge borrowers) and the weighted average deposit rate (what banks pay depositors). A high spread indicates high banking costs or profits at the expense of both depositors and borrowers. Bangladesh Bank monitors the spread and has taken measures to reduce it, including capping the lending rate at 9% (SMART rate + margin) to make credit more affordable.

question: During the final offensive in December 1971, Sector 11 forces advanced toward which strategic objective?

options.A: Chittagong Port, to prevent Pakistani forces from escaping by sea
options.B: Dhaka city from the north, in coordination with Indian paratroopers and the Kaderia Bahini
options.C: The Sylhet tea gardens, to capture the economically vital export industry intact
options.D: The Sundarbans, to secure the southwestern flank of the advancing allied forces

explanation: Sector 11's final objective was to advance on Dhaka from the north. After the Tangail Airdrop (11 December 1971) linked Indian paratroopers with Sector 11 forces and Kaderia Bahini, the combined force cut off Pakistani retreat routes and pushed south toward the capital. This northern pincer, coordinated with advances from the west, east, and northeast, surrounded Dhaka and forced the Pakistani surrender on 16 December.

question: According to Article 7(1) of the Constitution, where do all powers in the Republic belong?

options.A: To the Parliament, as the directly elected representatives of the nation
options.B: To the President, as the constitutional head of the Republic
options.C: To the people, and their exercise on behalf of the people shall be effected under this Constitution
options.D: To the Supreme Court, as the guardian and interpreter of the Constitution

explanation: Article 7(1) declares: 'All powers in the Republic belong to the people, and their exercise on behalf of the people shall be effected only under, and by the authority of, this Constitution.' This establishes popular sovereignty — the people are the ultimate source of all authority, and the Constitution is the framework through which that authority is exercised.

question: Which major Western newspaper published Anthony Mascarenhas's article 'Genocide' that exposed Pakistani atrocities to the world?

options.A: The Sunday Times of London, which published Mascarenhas's eyewitness account on 13 June 1971, shocking the international community
options.B: The New York Times, which ran the article as a front-page investigation in its Sunday edition
options.C: The Washington Post, which serialized the report over three consecutive days
options.D: The Guardian, which published it alongside photographs taken by French photojournalists

explanation: Anthony Mascarenhas, a Pakistani journalist, fled to London and published 'Genocide' in The Sunday Times on 13 June 1971. His first-hand account of the Pakistani military's atrocities shocked the world and turned Western public opinion against Pakistan. The article was read into the US Congressional Record and was a pivotal moment in the international awareness of the Bangladesh genocide.

question: What export target has Bangladesh set for its Ready-Made Garment sector?

options.A: $50 billion by 2030, focusing on product diversification, value addition, and expanding into non-traditional markets
options.B: $100 billion by 2025, aiming to surpass China as the world's largest garment exporter
options.C: $30 billion by 2035, reflecting conservative growth projections for the mature industry
options.D: $75 billion by 2041, aligned with the overall Vision 2041 development framework

explanation: The Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association has set a target of $50 billion in RMG exports by 2030. Achieving this requires: (1) Product diversification beyond basic garments to high-value items; (2) Moving up the value chain from cut-make-trim to design and branding; (3) Expanding into non-traditional markets beyond the EU and US; (4) Improving sustainability and compliance standards. The RMG sector currently exports approximately $40+ billion annually.
